days.cross_cutting_mbo_finding: MY OWN LENS'S CORE PREMISE IS REFUTED ON THIS EVIDENCE. The lens file states: 'The 06-10 ET catch-up window is where Monday decides; the overnight session is drift that the US morning either ratifies or reverses.' I measured the 06:00-10:00 ET window's contribution on every Monday available across two staged groups, off the realized continuous curves. It is NEGATIVE ON ALL FOUR: g22 0622 -710, g22 0629 -510, g23 0706 -50, g23 0713 -360 (median -435). The two adjacent sub-periods each split 2-2 (pre-06: +500 / -490 / +390 / -100; 10-close: -350 / -160 / +340 / +200). The window is the ONLY sub-period of a Monday that is unanimous in sign, and it is unanimous in the sell direction - including on the two Mondays that closed UP on the day (0622 +650, 0706 +100), where the window traded against the day's own direction. On my day specifically the window contributed -50 of a +880 realized advance: the advance happened before it (overnight and early morning, +390 from the open to 06:00) and after it (+340 from 10:00 to the close). The window did not decide the day and it did not ratify anything. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) The lens's RATIFICATION arm is 0 for 2 and should be retired: on this evidence the US morning does not ratify a positive overnight, it sells into it. (2) The lens's real object is the SEAM, not the window - 100 percent of the block's gap risk sits on Mondays (weekday |gap| <= 20 across 16 seams; weekend |gap| 1,210 / 50 / 580 / 360), and on my day the gap error alone (980) was 2.45x the day-level error the blind was scored on. A Monday specialist whose attention is on 06-10 is watching the quietest four hours of his own day. THE CAVEAT THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST: g22 and g23 sit inside a single downtrend (3.319 -> 2.916), so a unanimous sell window may be a regime sample rather than a structure. The falsifier is explicit and cheap: an up-trending fortnight in which the Monday 06-10 window is positive on 2 or more Mondays.

proposal_2.id: boundary.weekend_gap_wide_band_emission - SPLIT THE SIGN FROM THE BAND
proposal_2.claim: The play currently fuses a sign claim to a magnitude band and emits a one-sided band. Split it: emit the gap MAGNITUDE as a signless band from the sigma x book-state rung, and emit the gap SIGN as a separate, separately-scored instrument. Score the two independently.
proposal_2.evidence: My day is the clean demonstration. The magnitude arm was RIGHT (|actual gap| 580 sits inside the |150..700| band the play derived from a 0.5-1.0x era-degraded sigma, and the mid-book rung was correctly preferred to the 1.5-2.5x extreme rung). The sign arm was WRONG. Because the band is one-sided, a correct magnitude read scored as a 730 USD miss outside the near edge. Across the four weekend seams in g22+g23, the |150..700| band would contain |gap| on 2 of 4 (580, 360) and miss 2 (1,210, 50) - so the band's width is mediocre on its own and its usable content is being destroyed by a sign error it does not need to carry.

proposal_3.claim: SCOPE REFINEMENT to C's numb-class rule (which I corroborate out-of-sample), not a competing rule. A numb prior-session terminal coefficient bounds the next day's NET and says nothing useful about its RANGE. It is a net-suppressor, not a volatility-suppressor. A desk sizing a quiet day off it will be right about the close and badly wrong about the path.
proposal_3.evidence: Numb seams in g22+g23 (|k3_prev| <= 0.05), per instance: 0703->0706 net +100 on a range of 970 (ratio 9.7) with a 960 USD turn and a low 840 below the anchor; 0713->0714 net +200 range 780 (3.9); 0714->0715 net -60 range 760 (12.7); 0715->0716 net -20 range 1,450 (72.5). Against the non-numb days in the same two groups: median |net| 520 and median range 1,350, ratios 1.2 to 5.0. The numb class compresses the NET by 6.5x (median |net| 80 vs 520) but the RANGE by only 1.5x (875 vs 1,350). CORROBORATION of C's underlying rule: my seam is an independent instance in a day-class C did not sample (a 3-night holiday seam Monday) and it lands in class at +100 <= 200; all four numb seams in g22+g23 land in class.
proposal_3.n: 4 numb instances measured here spanning g22-g23, against a 15-session non-numb comparison in the same two groups. C reports further instances in g20, so the underlying rule spans three groups.
proposal_3.declared_weakness: My own instance measures k3_prev on 489 lots against C's stated >=500-lot floor. It is a boundary instance by 2 percent and should be counted as such.
proposal_3.scope: Next-day NET only. Explicitly silent on sign (C's own refusal, which I keep) and now explicitly silent on range.
proposal_3.falsifier: A numb seam (|k3_prev| <= 0.05, |ph3 flow| >= 500) whose next session both nets >= 700 USD and does so without an exogenous catalyst - which would break the net claim; or a run of numb seams whose ranges compress as hard as their nets, which would break this refinement.

If you have no independent number to compare, you have not decided anything - you have relayed. (2) EXECUTING A CONDITIONAL PRODUCES A LIMB STATE, NOT A SIGN. Resolving another specialist's test tells you what the AUTHOR would have concluded from your measurements. It does not tell you what YOU conclude, because you hold evidence the author did not - on my day, an unmasked balance channel, a realized COT print, a served prior-full-session tape and a Sunday stub. The correct product of a handed-down test is 'limb A pass, limb B unreadable, and here is my own read alongside'. (3) IF THEY DISAGREE, THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE FINDING AND BOTH NUMBERS SHIP. Emit your read, emit the table's verdict, emit which you took and why. That is a decision. Silently adopting the table is not, and it also destroys the evidence the next round needs - had my blind carried my own number beside E's verdict, this refine would have been able to score the acceptance itself rather than reconstruct it. (4) CHECK THE TEST'S ARMS BEFORE RUNNING IT: from the state you are in, was the failing branch reachable? On my day, once the weekend was warm, limb A passes by construction and limb B could only have failed on a demand collapse measured against a national holiday. A test with no reachable failing branch is not a test, it is a formality, and this check is cheap, blind-available and takes one minute. (5) A DECLARED-WEAK LIMB RESOLVES UNREADABLE, NOT PASS. If you cannot degrade a limb's vote inside the table's grammar, degrade its verdict. Binary tables have no weights; that is a property of the table, not permission to ignore the weakness. (6) AND THE THING NOT TO DO, which is what I did: never argue that following the table means the call was not yours. My blind's cross_cutting_note says the UP call was 'E's OWN conditional table resolving on realized weekend data, not a rejection of E'. Single ownership does not care where the sign came from. The Monday sign was mine whether I derived it or inherited it, and process credit and answer credit are separate ledgers - E's refine reaches the identical conclusion from the other side, noting his own DOWN-SMALL was right in sign 'ONLY because its own conditional was never executed'. Neither of us gets to bank the other's ledger.
target_3_the_chain_audit.what_must_be_preserved_from_this_chain: The failure must not be read as an argument against conditional handoffs. What is missing from the architecture is a single term: nothing in the chain asks whether the handed-down instrument measures the right quantity, and nothing requires the receiving owner to have an independent number on the record before the table is consulted. Those are two small additions to a chain that otherwise worked.

proposal_contribution.note: TEXT ONLY, no brain edit, per the run directive. Every item states its n and whether it spans groups. The general-mechanism bar is n>=2 SPANNING GROUPS and nothing here meets it, so nothing here is proposed for merge as a market play. Items 1-3 are OPERATING RULES about how a handed-down instrument is consumed - they are not market claims and do not carry a market n; their basis is the coordinator's own single-ownership guard plus one measured failure, and I say so rather than dressing them as findings. Items 4-6 are market/instrument observations with their n stated and their cross-group sweep named.

item_1_the_owners_read_precedes_the_verd.statement: A specialist who owns a day must produce and RECORD its own number, from its own lens and its own slice, BEFORE executing any handed-down conditional. Executing another specialist's test yields a LIMB STATE, never a sign. If the owner's read and the table's verdict disagree, both ship in the posterior along with which was taken and why; the disagreement is itself the measurement. A posterior whose sign is inherited must say so in the confidence field.
item_1_the_owners_read_precedes_the_verd.why_it_is_not_a_market_claim: It follows from the coordinator contract that already exists: the coordinator SELECTS one owner per day, never averages, and treats a wrong-owner posterior as a hard failure. Single ownership of the number and outsourcing of the sign are incompatible. This needs no market n because it asserts nothing about markets.
item_1_the_owners_read_precedes_the_verd.evidence: G23 0713. My blind posterior contains no independent number anywhere - the reasoning field opens by deriving the sign from E's table and explicitly disclaims authorship ('not by my override'). The cost is not only the 1,170 error: because no independent read was recorded, this refine cannot score the acceptance decision against an alternative and has to reconstruct it. n=1 measured failure, one block, one specialist.
item_1_the_owners_read_precedes_the_verd.cheap_forward_check: Mechanical, no new data: scan G17-G22 per-day posteriors for owned days whose reasoning derives its SIGN from an upstream specialist's verdict table or bias field, and score those days' direction hit-rate against days where the owner derived the sign in-file. item_2_a_declared_weak_limb_resolves_unr.statement: When a test limb's baseline or instrument is DECLARED contaminated - by the stager, by the owner, or by the state's own defect fields - the limb resolves UNREADABLE, not PASS and not FAIL. Weight-degradation in prose has no effect inside a binary verdict table; if the limb's vote cannot be degraded, its verdict must be. Corollary: MEASURABLE is not READABLE. A number served at the right period and the right age can still be unreadable if its comparator is contaminated.
item_2_a_declared_weak_limb_resolves_unr.evidence: G23 0713 limb B. A pinned the Sat-0704 comparator and flagged it in advance as Independence Day itself, writing that 'the INFORMATIVE outcome is a FAIL'. The limb passed at 43.5 vs 42.9 Bcf/d - +1.4% against a national holiday, a pass with no discriminating power. My blind explicitly recognised the softness ('gives the pass a built-in tailwind... CONFIRMING rather than amplifying') and then recorded a full PASS vote. MEASURED COUNTERFACTUAL: A's own unreadable-limb rule ('a passing limb A stays A-ONLY, never promote to full band on an unmeasured limb') routes the table to its A-ONLY branch - gap-only, no intraday lean - which at A's own low-gain seam class cuts my error from 1,170 to roughly 600-700. n=1 instance with a counterfactual computed from a rule already written in the staging file.

item_3_check_the_tests_arms_before_runni.statement: Before executing a handed-down conditional, ask whether its FAILING branch was reachable from the state you are actually in. If the evidence you are about to gather could only have produced one answer, the test is a formality and its verdict carries no information.
